newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rules out sharing disputed area with China.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rules out sharing disputed area with China.

text.p: Hanoi would not consider a production-sharing agreement with Beijing in the disputed offshore area where China is drilling, a senior official of the state oil and gas firm Petrovietnam said on Monday. "Vietnam would never sign a contract on production-sharing with China on its continental shelf," Petrovietnam director Vu Van Mao told reporters. "If someone came to your country and drilled, and then asked you to sign a contract, would you?"

Mao, director of Petrovietnam's petroleum information centre, said there could be no comparison made with overlapping maritime areas off Vietnam's southern coast, where sharing deals have been set up with neighbouring countries.

He said Hanoi's position in the row over the area, between China's Hainan Island and the coast of central Vietnam, was that the drilling rig and accompanying vessels must withdraw and that talks should be held to solve the issue peacefully.
His comments, made on the sidelines of an oil, gas and petrochemicals conference, echoed a statement made earlier by the foreign ministry.

The dispute between Hanoi and Beijing erupted earlier this month when Vietnam protested to China over the positioning of an exploration rig off the coast of central Vietnam. China responded that the area was in its own territory and that its action was beyond reproach.
